t: You are at the site of the Diorama in Regent's Park, a specialised theatre built in 1823 to show large, dramatized tableaux paintings as entertainment. It was designed by Augustus Charles Pugin, a French-born artist and architectural draughtsman who spent most of his adult life in England. He had trained at the Royal Academy Schools and worked as a draughtsman for the architect John Nash. Pugin later settled into a career as a commercial artist, working mainly for publishers of illustrated books, and he was also a skilful watercolourist.
